case studies

( Noura`s cases )

case study 01

Scaling a Saudi Furniture E-commerce Brand to 10X ROAS

Industry: Furniture & Home

clint : alsaada home

Market: Saudi Arabia

Platforms : meta,tiktok,google

Monthly Budget: SAR 30,000

Revenue Target: SAR 300,000

Primary Objective: Generate SAR 300,000 in monthly revenue

Challenge

  • Multiple Meta Pixels causing duplicate tracking.
  • Inaccurate conversion data and unreliable reporting.
  • Required to achieve 10X ROAS from a SAR 30K monthly budget.

My Strategy

Tracking Optimization

  • Audited the Meta Pixel setup.
  • Removed duplicate and incorrect pixels.
  • Rebuilt accurate conversion tracking.

Product Analysis

Segmented products into:

  • Seasonal Products
  • Fast-Moving Products
  • High-Profit Products

Campaign Strategy

  • Created separate campaigns for each product category.
  • Developed different ad angles based on customer intent.
  • Launched Saudi National Day promotional campaigns with discount offers.

Optimization Process

  • Daily campaign monitoring.
  • Budget reallocation based on ROAS.
  • Audience optimization.
  • Creative testing.
  • Product performance analysis.
  • Continuous scaling of winning campaigns.

Results

MetricResult
Monthly Ad SpendSAR 30,000
Revenue TargetSAR 300,000
Revenue AchievedSAR 300,000+
ROAS10X
Following Month11X ROAS

KEY TAKEAWAYS

  1. Accurate tracking comes before scaling.

    Fixing the measurement infrastructure allowed performance decisions to be based on reliable data.

  2. Product-level strategy matters.

    Not every product deserves the same budget or advertising angle.

  3. Seasonal demand can significantly improve performance.

    The Saudi National Day period was used as a strategic sales opportunity rather than simply a promotional event.

  4. Budget should follow performance.

    Instead of distributing spend equally, budget was continuously shifted toward stronger-performing products and campaigns.

  5. Continuous optimization creates scalability.

    The account improved from 10X to 11X ROAS as more data was collected and the strategy was refined.

case study 02

Building a High-Intent Patient Acquisition Strategy Across Egypt & Saudi Arabia

Client: Dr. Alaa Haggag

Specialization: Hair Transplantation & Aesthetic Medicine

Markets: Egypt & Saudi Arabia

Platforms : meta,tiktok,google

Monthly Budget: 60,000 EG

Primary Objective: Generate qualified patient inquiries and increase procedure bookings

Challenge

The doctor targeted both Egypt and Saudi Arabia, but Saudi patients had to travel to Egypt for their procedures, making audience quality and purchasing power critical.

Strategy

  • Segmented premium Egyptian areas including Sheikh Zayed, New Cairo, Heliopolis, Zamalek & 6th of October.
  • Focused Saudi targeting on Riyadh, Jeddah & Medina instead of wasting budget across the entire country.
  • Used real Saudi patients and testimonials to build trust and address travel-related objections.

Execution

Built separate audience and creative structures for each market and service, using patient experiences, testimonials, and conversion-focused messaging.

Optimization

Monitored campaigns daily, analyzed audience and creative performance, shifted budget toward high-quality segments, and continuously refreshed creatives to prevent fatigue.

Results

16 Hair Transplant Procedures in One Month

The campaign became one of the client’s successful patient acquisition channels.

KEY TAKEAWAYS

  1. High-ticket services require quality-focused targeting.

    The objective was not to generate the cheapest lead possible, but to attract people capable of becoming actual patients.

  2. Geography can be a powerful qualification tool.

    Premium areas were used as an indicator of purchasing power and audience quality.

  3. Social proof reduces friction.

    Real Saudi patient experiences helped address the major objection of traveling to Egypt.

  4. Creative fatigue must be managed continuously.

    Regular creative rotation helped maintain campaign performance.

  5. Different markets require different strategies.

    The Egyptian and Saudi campaigns were not treated as one audience or one campaign strategy.

case study 03

Gerash Medical Complex — Building a New Healthcare Brand

Market: Saudi Arabia

Platforms : meta,Snapchat

Monthly Budget: SAR 5,000

Location: Abu Arish, Jizan

Industry: Healthcare

Duration: 1+ Year

Challenge

Gerash Medical Complex was a new healthcare brand competing against long-established medical centers with stronger local recognition

strategy

  • Conducted detailed competitor analysis.
  • Analyzed competitor reviews, complaints, and customer feedback to identify market gaps.
  • Selected specific medical services to promote each month.
  • Aligned campaigns with doctor availability and seasonal demand.
  • Combined Reach, Awareness, Engagement & Messages campaigns to build visibility and generate bookings.

Execution

Focused campaigns geographically on the local market and created seasonal service campaigns, such as ENT services during relevant periods and dermatology/skin treatments during beauty-focused periods.

Optimization

Continuously analyzed campaign performance, audience response, message volume, service demand, and seasonal behavior, adjusting the monthly strategy accordingly.

Results

  • Established strong local brand visibility.
  • Expanded reach across Abu Arish and the wider Jizan market.
  • Achieved strong Google visibility for relevant local searches.
  • After the successful first branch, the client opened a new branch in Sabya and trusted me to manage its advertising as well.

KEY TAKEAWAYS

  1. New brands need visibility before conversion.

    For a new medical complex, building local awareness was essential before expecting consistent booking volume.

  2. Competitor reviews can become a strategic advantage.

    Customer complaints and positive reviews revealed market gaps that could be used to improve positioning.

  3. Healthcare advertising requires operational coordination.

    Campaigns must be aligned with doctor availability and booking capacity.

  4. Seasonal demand should influence the media plan.

    The promoted services changed according to customer needs and seasonal behavior.

  5. Long-term consistency creates business impact.

    The strongest proof of success was not only campaign performance but the client’s decision to expand and continue the partnership into a new branch.

case study 04

Saudi Bamboo Décor E-commerce Brand

Market: Saudi Arabia

Platforms: Meta Ads & TikTok Ads

Monthly Budget: SAR 7,000

Location: ryiadah

Industry: Decoration

CHALLENGE

The brand needed to scale sales in the Saudi market while identifying the highest-performing regions and audiences without wasting budget.

STRATEGY

  • Segmented the Saudi market into North, East, West, and Islands.
  • Analyzed regional performance and audience behavior.
  • Developed tailored creative angles for each audience segment.
  • Focused on Meta and TikTok as the primary acquisition channels.

EXECUTION

  • Built separate campaigns/ad sets for each geographic segment.
  • Tested different audiences, creatives, and messaging angles.
  • Monitored performance by region and campaign.
  • Continuously redistributed budget based on results.

OPTIMIZATION

  • Scaled high-performing regions and audiences.
  • Reduced spend on underperforming segments.
  • Tested new creative angles to maintain performance.
  • Optimized campaigns based on CPA, purchases, and overall efficiency.

RESULTS

Meta & TikTok became the strongest-performing acquisition channels,while geographic segmentation created a more efficient and scalable campaign structure.

KEY TAKEAWAYS

  • Geographic segmentation improved budget control.
  • Data-driven allocation reduced inefficient spend.
  • Continuous creative testing supported scalability.
  • Performance-based optimization unlocked stronger growth opportunities.
